notes: Whithersoever is read as a three-morpheme fusion of be, kol and asher (rules 30 and 35); the head could as defensibly be taken on kol.

Large-source-unit check: the three morphemes are contiguous and one English word carries the locative relation, the universal quantification and the relative alike, so no morpheme owns a part and the grouping is retained.
In the last clause the dative lahem is recast into the English subject, so the preposition is unrepresented and the suffix takes they (rule 40).
